code.bar_note: MEASURED FLOOR, not the 0.30 spec bar. The pre-Phase-1 baseline commit 579568d re-runs at 0.10 on the SAME live index, so the 0.30 was index drift, not a code regression: bin/lib/*.mjs is no longer in global.db, only stale graft/*.md cards remain. Restoring it needs a global.db rebuild, which was authorized and then blocked by a real 6.0 GB RAM guard (host had 5.7 GB); the decision on record is to record the floor rather than close anything.

fact.bar_note: First measured-reachable bar. Reached 0.90. The original 0.00 was structural only because 0 of 10 fact golds existed anywhere in the corpus; the golds are now 10 real facts extracted from the user own session logs, each verified present before use.

person.bar_note: First measured-reachable bar. Reached 1.00. The original 0.00 was structural only because 0 of 10 person queries named their own gold, and 3 of 10 golds were absent from people.db entirely.

regressions.default_kb_search_output: byte-identical to a golden captured before any production change (tests/kinds-default-identical.test.mjs, 2 pass)
regressions.code_slice_vs_0.30_spec_bar: NOT MET, and the bar itself is stale. See slices.code.bar_note.

review: four adversarial rounds; Phase 4 fixed 2 BLOCKERs and 3 MAJORs before this measurement
gold_set_note: The person and fact gold sets were rebuilt in Phase 4. As shipped in Phase 0, 0 of 10 person queries mentioned their own gold name and 0 of 10 fact golds existed anywhere in the corpus, so both 0.00s measured the gold set rather than retrieval. Every replacement gold is a real record, verified present in people.db / journal.db before use, and the integrity is now asserted by a test rather than assumed.
